name: hardening_verdict
verdict: PRACTICAL_ADVANCE on tkgl-polecat and tkgl-smallpedia: the claim survives on both datasets under the pre-registered rule (C1, C2 and C3 pass on both two-strongest bases of each dataset). Qualification: on the strongest bases the pool-widening share of the gain is small (HRCOV - HR = +0.0129 on polecat TiRGN, +0.0029 on smallpedia TiRGN); most of the margin over the recurrency controls comes from the history re-ranker.

deviations: HisRES (arXiv:2405.10621) was not run: no public code was found (arXiv PDF has no code link; GitHub search for the name / full title returned nothing; paperswithcode is outside the network allowlist and was not requested). The base pool is RE-GCN, LogCL, TiRGN.

Official TGB RecB script was not re-run in train mode (projected > 8 h on polecat); the vectorised re-implementation was verified per query against the official default-mode CSV (22 of 533,472 valid queries differ) and reproduces the TGB 2.0 leaderboard train-mode rows to the third decimal (polecat 0.198, smallpedia 0.605).
The rule's reference row for smallpedia RecB (0.604, quoted from the pilot report) is 0.605 on the TGB 2.0 leaderboard; the report uses 0.605. Not decision-relevant.

Polecat RE-GCN and LogCL are the pilot-1 checkpoints with the fixed 12-epoch budget (no valid-best epoch selection). A per-epoch valid-curve diagnostic could not run: the 24 GB RTX 4090 runs out of memory at history 10, and the 96 GB card on serverA (GPU 0) was occupied by other users when the job checked it (it aborted by design). Polecat valid-best epoch selection is applied to TiRGN only.

TiRGN on polecat uses history L = 10 (authors' value) on serverA GPU 0 (96 GB), not the L in {6, 4, 3} fallback planned for the 24 GB card. The planned fallback did not produce a model: L = 6 passed a 40-step probe on serverB but ran out of memory in its first full epoch (job). The serverA L = 10 run (job) is therefore the only TiRGN polecat model, and it is the reported base. This removes, rather than adds, a deviation from the authors' configuration.

TiRGN is trained with entity prediction only (relation_prediction = False, no static graph), as in pilot 2. In that configuration TiRGN's own get_loss objective (0.7 * entity NLL + 0.3 * relation NLL + static loss) reduces to 0.7 * entity NLL, because the relation and static terms are identically zero. The chunked decoder loss used on polecat reproduces that objective exactly.

TiRGN polecat pipeline stages after training ran on mixed hosts because serverA GPU 0 became occupied by other users: exact list lookup on the serverB RTX 4090 (193 s; a CPU lookup on serverA was cancelled after 1.7 h), features and HR/HRCOV training on serverA CPU (16 threads), controls and the official test pass on the serverB RTX 4090.

TiRGN polecat: the pilot's lookup-vs-dump exact-rank agreement check (> 0.99, calibrated for same-GPU runs) failed across GPUs (dump on the RTX PRO 6000, lookup on the RTX 4090: 0.980 valid / 0.978 test). All disagreements are deep near-tie blocks (median gold rank about 121k of 150,931; gold log p equal to 1.4e-5; MRR equal to 1e-8; top-1 identical), so the threshold was lowered to 0.97 for this base only (diagnostic hardening/diag/rank_agree.py). Not tuned on any outcome.
LogCL re-tuning grid on smallpedia is time-ordered only (no shuffled-snapshot arm): LogCL's global copy-history is order-dependent.
LogCL re-tuned smallpedia selected the last epoch of the 12-epoch cap (valid still rising by 0.0002 at epoch 12).

Official evaluator applied batch-wise: per-query reciprocal ranks computed with the evaluator's formula on the official negatives; each batch's mean compared with Evaluator.eval (largest recorded deviation 0.0 on every pass; recorded, not asserted).
HR_RB / HRCOV_RB (RecB score features) evaluated with the harness evaluator only (declared secondary, not in the decision).
Polecat blend / pool selection used the pilots' 200k valid sample (rng 12345), as pre-registered; smallpedia used the full valid split.

HR / HRCOV on the pilot bases are the pilot re-ranker models (smallpedia promoted lists of seeds 1-2 regenerated from the saved seed models, rank agreement >= 0.99999); new bases (smallpedia re-tuned RE-GCN / LogCL, polecat TiRGN) were trained with the unchanged pilot recipe.
About 9 h of SSH outage (both hosts) delayed collection; jobs kept running and failed harvests were recovered from the job directories on disk.

open_issues: Polecat RE-GCN / LogCL valid-best epochs not established: the per-epoch valid diagnostic OOMs on the 24 GB RTX 4090 at history 10, and serverA GPU 0 was occupied by other users (job aborted by design). Re-run pc_epoch_curve_serverA.sh when GPU 0 is idle. Not decision-relevant for polecat: TiRGN (valid-best epoch) is the strongest base.

Pool-widening share of the HRCOV gain is small on strong bases (HRCOV - HR +0.0129 polecat TiRGN, +0.0029 smallpedia TiRGN vs +0.036 to +0.090 on weak bases); the pilot-1 mechanism statement ('gain = history-aware pool widening') should be restated as 'history re-ranking, plus pool widening on weak bases'.
Published rows above which HRCOV lands (CountTRuCoLa 0.256 / 0.644, NHCTE 0.245 / 0.618) were not re-run under our evaluator; the comparison is cross-paper.
HisRES not compared (no public code found).
Official TGB RecB train-mode script not re-run (projected > 8 h on polecat); the re-implementation matches the leaderboard rows.

RecB score as a re-ranker feature hurts on smallpedia TiRGN (HR_RB - HR -0.027, HRCOV_RB - HRCOV -0.012); hypothesised cause (lambda/alpha selected in-sample on the re-ranker's fitting split) untested. RB arms not run on TiRGN polecat or the re-tuned smallpedia bases.
LogCL re-tuned on smallpedia selected the last epoch of the 12-epoch cap; longer training untested. Our RE-GCN on smallpedia (0.4825 re-tuned) stays below the TGB 2.0 RE-GCN row (0.594).
HRCOV_ST_NODIRECT not run on the re-tuned smallpedia bases (secondary).
